Evaluate WGCNA module preservation and network stability

rna_wgcna_stability.Rd

Evaluates the preservation of co-expression modules, the stability of module membership (kME), and the conservation of intramodular hub genes between two experimental groups using independently reconstructed WGCNA networks.

Networks are reconstructed using the original WGCNA configuration stored in the project. Module preservation is assessed using permutation-based statistics, while kME correlations and hub gene overlap provide complementary measures of network stability. All comparisons are performed bidirectionally, using each group as the reference network.

Usage

rna_wgcna_stability(
  project,
  group = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  n_permutations = 200,
  hub_quantile = 0.9,
  threads = NULL,
  plot = TRUE,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

An rna_project object containing a previously constructed WGCNA network generated by rna_wgcna.

group

Optional character vector specifying exactly two experimental groups to compare. Both groups must be represented among the samples used in the original network. If NULL, groups are automatically identified when exactly two are available. Defaults to NULL.

reference

Optional character string specifying the reference group. The other selected group is automatically assigned as the comparison group. If NULL, the first selected group is used. Defaults to NULL.

n_permutations

Integer specifying the number of permutations used for module preservation analysis. Larger values provide more stable estimates but increase computational requirements. Defaults to 200.

hub_quantile

Numeric value between 0 and 1 defining the quantile used to identify hub genes based on absolute kME values. For example, 0.90 selects approximately the top 10\ module. Defaults to 0.90.

threads

Optional positive integer specifying the number of threads used during network reconstruction. If NULL, the default WGCNA behavior is used. Defaults to NULL.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, generates a bar plot of module preservation Zsummary statistics, including conventional preservation thresholds. Defaults to TRUE.

save

Logical. If TRUE, attaches the analysis result to the project under analyses$wgcna_stability and invisibly returns the updated project. Otherwise, invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_stability_result. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

If save = TRUE, invisibly returns the updated rna_project object.

If save = FALSE, invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_stability_result, containing:

  • preservation: interpretable module preservation statistics for both comparison directions.

  • preservation_raw: complete output from modulePreservation, including permutation results.

  • kME_stability: gene-module membership correlations and associated comparison information.

  • hub_stability: hub overlap, Jaccard indices, and associated module statistics.

  • networks: independently reconstructed WGCNA networks, including module assignments and eigengenes.

  • parameters: selected groups, sample counts, network configuration, and analysis parameters.

  • timestamp: date and time of analysis.

Input requirements

The original WGCNA result must contain the expression matrix and network configuration required for independent network reconstruction.

Sample metadata must contain unique Sample identifiers and a Group column. Sample identifiers must match the expression matrix row names. Metadata are automatically aligned to the expression matrix, and only samples included in the original network are considered.

Missing or empty group assignments are not allowed, and each selected group must contain at least 20 samples. The original set of WGCNA genes is retained without additional filtering.

Analysis

Independent networks are reconstructed for each selected group using the original WGCNA configuration. Module assignments may therefore differ between groups.

Three complementary stability measures are evaluated:

  • Module preservation: assessed using modulePreservation, which evaluates the conservation of module topology between reference and comparison networks. Zsummary values below 2 indicate weak evidence of preservation, values between 2 and 10 indicate moderate evidence, and values above 10 indicate strong evidence. These thresholds are empirical guidelines rather than formal significance cutoffs.

  • Module membership stability: evaluated using Pearson correlations between gene-level kME values calculated relative to reference module eigengenes in both groups. Higher correlations indicate greater conservation of gene-module relationships.

  • Hub gene stability: assessed by comparing the genes with the highest absolute kME values in each reference module. Hub overlap and the Jaccard index quantify the conservation of selected hub genes between groups.

All analyses are performed bidirectionally, using each group as the reference in turn. Grey modules are excluded from the interpretable preservation summary but retained in the raw WGCNA output.

Interpretation

Module preservation, kME stability, and hub overlap describe different aspects of network organization. A module may retain its overall topology while exhibiting changes in gene-module relationships or hub identity. Conversely, conserved hub genes do not necessarily indicate preservation of the entire module structure.

These measures do not establish network identity, exclude differential co-expression, or demonstrate causal relationships. Results should be interpreted in the context of sample size, experimental design, and potential confounding factors.

The function performs pairwise comparisons and does not implement formal differential network analysis, consensus network construction, or statistical adjustment for experimental covariates and repeated measurements.

References

Langfelder P, Horvath S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-559

Langfelder P, Luo R, Oldham MC, Horvath S. (2011). Is my network module preserved and reproducible? PLoS Computational Biology, 7(1), e1001057. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1001057
